title: What the Young-Driver Surcharge on a Keyturn Trip Booking Comes To
content:
The surcharge is the effective surcharge rate taken on the amount charged over, brought to the nearest cent again once that has been done.

**The amount charged over.** The amount charged over is the base-rate line standing on the Keyturn Trip Booking reservation — every line raised for the base rate, taken together and as each was raised, a credit or a reversal raised against one of them being a line of its own and not taken off it — spread evenly over the days of the reserved period and taken for each day charged. The days of the reserved period are counted from the first day of that period to the last, both days counted. The daily figure the spreading gives is brought to the nearest cent, and the amount charged over is brought to the nearest cent in its turn.

**The quantities that enter it.** The standard surcharge rate is 15 per cent. The days charged are the days the trip has already run, counted from the day the trip actually started to the day the surcharge is raised with that day counted. The standard protection, conduct and additional-driver adjustments are each nil, which is to say 0 percentage points.

**The effective rate.** The effective surcharge rate is the surcharge rate with the protection adjustment, the conduct adjustment and the additional-driver adjustment applied to it, each of them in percentage points and all of them added together to the rate before the rate is taken on anything; where that leaves a rate below nothing, no surcharge is owed.

### Worked through on hypothetical figures

*Hypothetical inputs: a single line of 1200.00 USD raised for the base rate on a reservation whose reserved period runs 20 days; the trip actually started 9 days before the day the surcharge is raised.*

The base-rate line of 1200.00 USD spread over the 20 days of the reserved period gives a daily figure of 60.00 USD, which is already at the cent. The days charged are the days the trip has already run counted to the day the surcharge is raised with that day counted: 10 days. Sixty dollars taken for each of those 10 days gives an amount charged over of 600.00 USD.

The surcharge rate is 15 per cent. The three adjustments are each 0 percentage points, so all of them added to the rate leave the effective surcharge rate at 15 per cent. Fifteen per cent taken on 600.00 USD is 90.00 USD, and brought to the nearest cent once that has been done the surcharge stands at **90.00 USD**.

*The same reservation, where the base rate was raised as two lines of 700.00 USD and 500.00 USD on different days, and a credit of 45.00 USD was afterwards raised against the first of them.* The two base-rate lines are taken together as each was raised, giving 1200.00 USD; the credit is a line of its own and is not taken off either of them, so the amount spread is the same 1200.00 USD.

Note the order: the percentage points are added to the rate first, and only then is the resulting rate taken on the amount charged over. The rate is never taken on the amount once for each adjustment.
